headline: Resolution would have canceled an Education Department rule on federal student loans, but the Senate did not take it up.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a Department of Education rule called "Reimagining and Improving Student Education-Federal Student Loan Program Final Regulations." If adopted and signed, the rule would have had no legal effect. The Department also could not have issued a substantially similar rule unless Congress later passed a law allowing it. No official summary is available, so the specific loan changes in the rule are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: People who have or plan to take out federal student loans
who_it_affects.how: The federal student loan rules in this regulation would have been canceled for them.
The Department would have lost this rule and been barred from issuing a substantially similar one without new approval from Congress.
